log.question: Is spending on track?
log.final_text:
Spending is below plan in this 20-Gram-Panchayat sample: costed activities are Rs 51.96 crore below plan, while approved activities are Rs 41.61 crore below plan. These gaps are spread across multiple Gram Panchayats, with Biswamathpur recording the largest amounts for both costed activities at Rs 7.23 crore below plan and approved activities at Rs 6.74 crore below plan, followed by Kalimela at Rs 5.90 crore and Rs 5.46 crore below plan respectively. 

Theme 6 - Self-sufficient Infrastructure in Village is Rs 20.13 crore below plan, also without a single Gram Panchayat dominating; Sharagada accounts for Rs 3.36 crore and Biswamathpur for Rs 2.66 crore below plan. Across districts, Bargarh and Ganjam have the lowest spending measured against plan in 6/7 LSDG themes; for Theme 4 - Water Sufficient Village, the lowest are Ganjam and Malkangiri.

Rural housing presents a more concentrated exception: it is Rs 2.23 crore below plan, of which Boipariguda accounts for 95.7%, or Rs 2.13 crore, despite holding 2.0% of the 305 activities; its spending-to-plan ratio is 0.0%. This makes Boipariguda’s rural-housing records a specific priority for reconciliation, alongside broader review of the distributed gaps in costed, approved and infrastructure activities.

Its plan- and sanction-based spending is also unevenly distributed across activity statuses, unlike the pattern in most Gram Panchayats. 

Chikilli is the broadest distributional outlier. It alone differs from the 19/20 pattern for plan-based spending across fund components, and for sanction-based spending across focus areas, output types, fund components and fiscal years. Chikilli also differs in sanction-based spending across types of work and activity statuses. Laxmipur is a narrower outlier, with uneven plan-based spending across activity statuses and uneven sanction-based spending across both activity statuses and types of work. 

Other differences concern which categories record the lowest spending against plan. Maintenance and New/Fresh are lowest among work types in 16/20 Gram Panchayats; Haldikudar, Itipur, Karuabahal and 1 other Gram Panchayat follow different patterns. Code 101 is lowest among output types in 17/20 Gram Panchayats, while Code 105 is lowest in Andhrua, Itipur and Sharagada. These category-level exceptions indicate where records and local practices may merit checking, but do not by themselves establish differences in total spending.
